A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Planning/VPRL study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v2 Appendices A–D correspond to v3 Appendices D–G, with additional statements and analyses in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original navigation experiments on FrozenLake, Maze, and MiniBehavior, including benchmark scores, training ablations, error analysis, and out-of-distribution results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds an intermediate-image quality control, tokenizer reconstruction examples, and inference token-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The LVM-based visual planner, random-trajectory initialization, GRPO optimization, dynamics interpreter, and progress rewards remain unchanged. Ground-truth intermediate frames are introduced as an evaluation control, while alternative reward mechanisms are discussed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use FrozenLake, Maze, and MiniBehavior with the same grid coverage, enlarged-grid evaluations, and masked-input examples. The new image-quality control reuses FrozenLake environments and task requirements; it changes the feedback procedure within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The Gemini, Qwen direct/CoT/SFT/GRPO, VPFT, and VPFT* comparison methods are retained in their corresponding experiments. The new cost tables reuse existing comparator sets, and Table 11 compares VPRL under two intermediate-frame settings.

E3.justification: v3 adds a FrozenLake control that replaces self-generated intermediate frames with environment-rendered frames during inference, plus evaluation of average generated-token counts. Existing splits, training budgets, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Section 3 clarifies state-based EM/PR matching without establishing a change to the earlier scoring procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix F.7 adds a tokenizer reconstruction case study and an intermediate-frame quality control to investigate image artifacts and planning sensitivity. Appendix F.8 adds computational-cost analysis through token usage. Existing initialization ablations, error analyses, and distribution-shift tests are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across groups for the training-reward curves in Figure 7, with the same Gaussian-smoothing description. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the new comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results. New Table 11 reports 92.1% EM and 93.4% PR with environment-rendered frames, alongside the retained self-generated-frame results of 91.6% and 93.2%. Tables 12–13 add token costs, including a cross-task average of 1082.5 for each visual planner versus 1178.6 for Gemini 2.5 Pro.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the reward partition, and the EM/PR formulas are retained. The added explanation of environment-state equality clarifies existing metric notation; no new or substantively revised theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about purely visual planning, two-stage VPRL, superiority over textual planning, and improved generalization. The stated 27% average EM advantage is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 attributes image artifacts to the tokenizer, interprets dynamics penalties as implicit format constraints, and argues that planning tolerates imperfect intermediate images. It also interprets the new token costs and expands the limitations discussion to emphasize reliable progress signals in complex environments and possible trajectory-level success feedback.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents state-level EM/PR matching and the new frame-substitution and token-count procedures. Appendix C adds a reproducibility roadmap and a promise to release all data and scripts upon acceptance. The existing code link, dataset construction, training hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Visual Sketchpad, MVoT, reinforcement learning for visual reasoning, and action-conditional generative models remain the same. Numbered citations become author–year citations, with corresponding bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain intact. v3 adds limited explanatory and supplementary prose, acknowledgements, and LLM-use, ethics, and reproducibility statements; it also updates affiliations, heading styles, citations, and appendix lettering.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 16 and Tables 11–13 while retaining the earlier figures, examples, and tables. The conference template changes title/header styling and float placement, with limited table-emphasis and case-study formatting adjustments; the overall single-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evaluation transparency through clearer EM/PR matching, the image-quality investigation in Figure 16 and Table 11, and systematic token accounting in Tables 12–13 instead of relying solely on an anecdotal cost discussion. The expanded limitations also better identify challenges in extending reward evaluation. These are useful but bounded gains: token counts do not establish runtime affordability, and the new accuracy control lacks uncertainty estimates.
